title: I built a simplified PUBG almost entirely with Codex
author: Due-Razzmatazz-4835
selftext:
Hi, I'm a Unity developer and recently I've been experimenting with something a bit unusual.

I built a simplified PUBG-style game mostly by myself, using Codex for almost all of the coding.

It includes things like parachuting, shooting, weapons, inventory, loot, grenades, healing, AI players, a shrinking zone, multiplayer-style synchronization, and a fake server so the whole thing can run offline.

I started it mainly as an experiment: I wanted to see how far one developer could go if AI handled most of the actual code writing.

My role was mostly deciding the architecture, breaking down problems, testing, debugging, and telling Codex what to change. When something became messy, I would usually refactor the design rather than keep fixing individual bugs.

The interesting part is that it actually became a fairly large working project, not just a small prototype.

I'm curious if anyone else here is working this way — using AI not just for autocomplete or small scripts, but for most of the code in a real game project.

comments.author: MrDankyStanky
comments.body: Yeah I've been messing with Claude code the same way. I have a pretty cool base for a game already and it's only been 4 or 5 days of work.

replies.author: Due-Razzmatazz-4835
replies.body: Yeah, AI has sped things up a lot. What used to take weeks can now take just a few days.I have made several demos now.

comments.author: DaedalusRaistlin
comments.body: I'm worried about people cheating in browser multiplayer games. It's just easier, less ways to prevent it, no anticheat services exist for the browser that I know of. Maybe I need to get AI working on it...
